transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Gomez (Pegasus Procurement), Mark Davis (Pegasus Legal), Priya Narang (Pegasus CTO), Luis Romero (Pegasus Cloud)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll just do a quick agenda - MSA/DPA redlines, SLA matrix, pricing for dedicated vs hosted, and onboarding next steps. Ravi's going to cover the technical items.
[00:18] Elena Gomez: Thanks Maya, yeah goal for today is to get alignment on legal points and the SLA numbers so we can take to execs next week, and also confirm any blockers for pilot.
[00:34] Ravi Patel: Quick intro from our side, Ravi SE on infra, I'll run through the architecture we propose for Pegasus and call out the VPC/KMS bits.
[00:50] Mark Davis: Hi, I'm Mark, legal - mostly interested in data residency, retention, indemnity language and DPA obligations.
[01:05] Priya Narang: Priya here, CTO - main things: latency targets, throughput, and whether we need Dedicated capacity or can start hosted. Also SSO integration and audit logs.

Summary (auto):
- Customer requested redlines to MSA/DPA, clarification on SLAs (uptime, latency SLOs), and pricing breakdown for Dedicated capacity and committed tiers.
- Action items assigned for redlines, benchmark, and security Qs.

[05:12] Maya Chen: On the MSA we typically accept most commercial redlines, Mark, can you highlight the top 3 items you want changed?
[05:30] Mark Davis: Sure, top three: tighter data return/destruction language, stronger liability cap carveouts for data breach, and a clear subprocessor list and notification obligation. Also need to confirm SOC2/ISO references.
[05:58] Maya Chen: Understood - we can provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO certs, and the DPA can include a subprocessor schedule. For liability caps, we can propose a limited carve for data breaches - will add language.
[06:20] Elena Gomez: Also, can we get KMS/HSM options specified? We have clients that require customer-managed keys.
[06:34] Ravi Patel: Yes, Pegasus can use customer KMS in Private deployment or Dedicated via VPC with CMEK. In hosted we support bring-your-own-key via our KMS integrations for certain enterprise tiers. There's some caveat on key rotation windows, we'll document.

[09:00] Priya Narang: Latency - our user flows need sub-200ms tail p50/p95 for short prompts. Is that realistic on Redwood hosted or do we need Dedicated?
[09:18] Ravi Patel: For sub-200ms p95 on real traffic, Dedicated with pinned GPU pools is the safest route. Hosted can achieve low latency for small models and cached flows, but p95 under load is variable. We can show benchmark numbers.
[09:39] Priya Narang: OK, we might start with hosted for experiments but want a plan to move to Dedicated. Pricing needs to show both.

[12:10] Elena Gomez: On SLA, we need 99.9% monthly uptime for production endpoints and defined credits for breaches. Also retention of audit logs for 12 months.
[12:27] Maya Chen: We offer SLA tiers - 99.9% as standard on Dedicated with an SLA credit table. For hosted, higher tiers available for enterprise customers. We'll share the SLA matrix doc. Audit log retention can be extended as an add-on.

[15:05] Mark Davis: On DPA, are you able to commit to data deletion timelines after contract termination? Our policy is 90 days to ensure downstream processes complete.
[15:20] Ravi Patel: Standard is 60 days, but we can discuss 90 days in the DPA for Pegasus. We'll note any operational constraints.

[20:00] Elena Gomez: We received redlines from our side earlier, some were quite detailed, Maya have you seen them?
[20:12] Maya Chen: Yes, thanks Elena. We'll produce a redline summary that maps each requested change to our proposed language. Expect that by Friday.

[23:30] Priya Narang: Security review - we need to know encryption at rest, in transit, key admin roles, and whether logs include PII. Also do you provide audit trails for model updates and rollbacks?
[23:50] Ravi Patel: Encryption in transit TLS 1.2+, at rest AES-256. For Dedicated/Private, keys can be customer-managed. Audit trails for model rollouts are in Console, with versioning and rollout history. Logs are configurable; we can mask PII and we keep event logs separate from inference payloads.

[28:10] Luis Romero: On network topology - if we do VPC Private deployment, what's the expected network egress and peering setup?
[28:25] Ravi Patel: For VPC, we support private endpoints and VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink equivalent. Egress depends on usage but we can provide estimated bandwidth. We'll need your network team for a short checklist.

[33:00] Maya Chen: Pricing - high level, two parts: committed Dedicated monthly fee for reserved GPU pools, plus per-token usage on top for bursts. For hosted, it's purely usage-based with volume discounts.
[33:20] Elena Gomez: Can you share a model for our expected 5M tokens/month baseline and a 2x burst?
[33:32] Ravi Patel: We'll produce a pricing worksheet with scenarios: Hosted baseline, Dedicated with 1/3/6-month commits, and cost per 1k tokens. Also show quantization/throughput tuning savings.

[37:45] Mark Davis: Compliance items: do you support SSO via SAML/SCIM, role-based access, and org-level audit export? Our auditors will ask.
[37:58] Maya Chen: Yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning on enterprise plans, RBAC in Console, and audit export via syslog/S3. We'll include docs.

[42:10] Elena Gomez: On the MSA clause about subcontractors, we need notification and an opportunity to object to specific subprocessors.
[42:28] Maya Chen: We maintain a subprocessor list and provide notice; we can add a 30-day review period for Pegaus to flag critical concerns.

[46:00] Priya Narang: For the pilot, tech checklist: sample dataset, expected QPS, target latencies, and a contact for network config. We'll want a 2-week bench and a one-week ramp.
[46:20] Ravi Patel: We'll define the pilot scope in the technical onboarding doc. Ravi (SE) will own the bench and share results.

[50:10] Elena Gomez: Anything else on indemnity/limitation of liability? We need carveouts for gross negligence and data breach.
[50:25] Maya Chen: We can discuss limited carveouts; our legal team will propose language that balances both sides.

[55:00] Maya Chen: OK recap and next steps - I'll send the MSA/DPA redline summary by 2026-04-02, Ravi will run benchmarks and share by 2026-04-05, pricing worksheet and SLA matrix to be shared by Tuesday. Mark, you'll send any remaining legal Qs by 2026-04-01.
[55:20] Mark Davis: Sounds good.
[55:30] Priya Narang: We'll review internally and get back on decision timeline this week.
[55:40] Elena Gomez: Thanks all.
[55:50] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule pilot kickoff for April 6th.
[56:05] Call ends.
